chunks: This is not knowledge of the unseen
Rather, it is learning from the One who has knowledge
And indeed, the knowledge of the unseen is the knowledge of the Hour
And what Allah, Glory be to Him, enumerated by His saying

Indeed, Allah is with Him the knowledge of the Hour and He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow. And no soul knows in what land it will die..

key_terms.عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ: Knowledge of the Hour (Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Prophet's knowledge of the unseen and God's absolute knowledge of the unseen?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) distinguishes between the acquired knowledge of the Prophet and Imams, which is derived from divine revelation, and the absolute, exclusive knowledge of the unseen (Al-Ghayb) that belongs solely to Allah. By citing Surah Luqman, he clarifies that while prophets possess extensive knowledge, the specific 'knowledge of the unseen' often refers to the Hour and other enumerated matters like the rain and the wombs, which remain with God. This distinction reinforces the Shia theological view of the Imams' infallible but derivative knowledge, preventing the confusion of their status with absolute divinity.

en.sayed-ali-raza: This is not knowledge of hidden things (‘ilmu’l-ghayb ), [3]
these matters have been acquired from him (namely in Prophet) who knew them.
As regard knowledge of hidden things, that means knowledge of the Day of Judgement,
and the things covered by Allāh in the verse :
Verily, Allāh is He with Whom is the knowledge of the Hour . . . (Qur’ān, 31:34)
